data.title: SWFT theme: small white fluffy things
data.body: Style the app toward the SWFT origin theme — small, white, fluffy things that bring unexpected delight. Initial pass is styling only. Future phases may add frontend tech for richer visual effects.

data.title: Replace default Leaflet pins with white CircleMarkers
data.body: Swap L.marker() for L.circleMarker() in addMarker(). Use white fill, no stroke (or very subtle), radius = Math.max(41, window.innerHeight / 10). fillColor white, fillOpacity 0.85, weight 0 or weight 1 with pale grey stroke for visibility on light map tiles.

data.title: Audit map tile style for theme fit
data.body: Research softer tile options (CartoDB Positron, Stamen Watercolor, muted OSM variants) that complement white markers and a dreamy, whimsical aesthetic. No change yet — produce a recommendation only.

data.title: Design overall SWFT visual language
data.body: Define a cohesive visual language: colour palette (whites, soft pinks, sky blues, pale yellows), typography, UI chrome style (minimal, airy). Produces a short design brief to guide future UI work. Consider whether additional frontend tech (lightweight animation lib, CSS custom properties, canvas overlay) is needed.

data.title: Restyle UI chrome to match theme
data.body: Apply the visual language from the design brief to UI chrome: controls, future popups/notes UI, attribution. Keep it minimal and airy.

data.title: Button: clear all SWFTs
data.body: Add a UI button styled to the SWFT visual language that clears all markers from the map. Client-side only — removes all CircleMarker layers without deleting from Supabase. Consider placement, icon/label, and hover/active states consistent with the airy, minimal theme.

data.title: Button: go to current location
data.body: Add a UI button that pans/zooms the map to the users current GPS location using the browser Geolocation API. Handle permission denied and unavailable cases gracefully. Style consistent with SWFT visual language.

data.title: Button: go to most recent SWFT
data.body: Add a UI button that pans the map to the most recently added SWFT marker. Track the latest marker position in JS state. Style consistent with SWFT visual language.

data.title: Button: toggle auto-follow new SWFTs
data.body: Add a toggle button that enables/disables auto-panning the map to each new SWFT as it arrives via Supabase Realtime. Default off. Indicate active state visually. Style consistent with SWFT visual language.

data.title: Load existing SWFTs on page init
data.body: On map load, fetch all existing rows from the clicks table and render them as CircleMarkers. Currently the app only shows markers arriving via Realtime in the current session — a fresh load shows an empty map. This is a prerequisite for go-to-most-recent and auto-follow to be meaningful from the start of a session. Use a single Supabase select() call ordered by created_at desc; store the most-recent lat/lng in JS state for XOM5DA to use.

data.title: Implement soft tile layer
data.body: Swap the default OpenStreetMap tile layer for the tile recommended by the audit task (IW5S5U). Likely CartoDB Positron or similar — light, minimal, low-colour. Ensure attribution is correct per tile provider license. No visual language definition needed here — just the swap and attribution.

Swap L.marker() for L.circleMarker() in addMarker(). White fill (fillColor: #fff, fillOpacity: 0.88), no border (weight: 0). Radius: window.innerHeight / 10 in pixels — on a typical mobile screen (~800px) this gives ~80px, on desktop (~900px) ~90px. CircleMarker radius stays constant in screen pixels regardless of zoom level, which is the right behaviour. Test that markers are visible on both light and dark map tiles; add a 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.15) stroke if needed for contrast on light tiles.

Add a UI button that clears all CircleMarker layers from the map client-side (no Supabase delete). Note: new SWFTs arriving via Realtime will still appear after a clear — the button resets the current view, not the stream. Consider whether to also pause the stream while cleared, or simply let new ones appear fresh. Style to SWFT visual language (task R44EOW). Scope of clear: local session view only.

Define the cohesive SWFT visual language to guide all subsequent UI tasks. Outputs a short written design brief (can live in AGENTS.md or a design-notes file). Cover: (1) colour palette — white, soft pastels, no hard blacks; (2) typography — if any UI text appears; (3) button style — shape, size, touch target, hover/active states, placement on map; (4) motion — whether subtle fade-in on marker appearance fits the theme; (5) whether any additional frontend tech is needed (animation lib, CSS custom props, canvas overlay). Tile audit (IW5S5U) and white-dot implementation (OW7EMA) must be done first to inform decisions.
